chunks: And it is narrated from al-Fuḍayl, Zurārah, and Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام.
That they asked him about buying meat from the markets while it is not known what the butchers do, so he said: "Eat, if it is in the markets of the Muslims, and do not ask about it."

key_terms.الْقَصَّابُونَ: butchers who prepare and sell meat
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمِينَ: Muslims, whose market context is legally significant
key_terms.شِرَاءِ: the act of purchasing or buying

ai.seo_question: Can meat bought from Muslim markets be eaten without investigating how the butchers slaughtered it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding purchasing meat from Muslim markets when the exact practices of the butchers are unknown. It indicates that meat found in the markets of the Muslims is to be treated as permissible, without requiring further inquiry.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4185 - And it is narrated from Al-Fudayl, Zurara, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as):

They asked him about buying meat from the markets without knowing what the butchers do.
Imam (as) said: "Eat if it is in the markets of the Muslims, and do not ask about it."
